about: CHAIN saga_neustria_west: the saint who left his island. Saint Philibert's monastery on Herio (Noirmoutier), 830 to 836: the abbot's wall, the fight on the saint's feast in 835, the king's leave to move the body, and the seventh day of June 836, with a coda at Saint-Denis about 838 to 840. Fourteen cards: nine steps, four endings and the coda. Endings: the saint carried to the mainland (what happened); the island and its rakers (what happened, seen from the sand); the saint stays behind a manned wall (history changed); the monks' lead sold on the Seine (the Breton lead thieves of Ermentarius, Miracles I.81). Words: Data/writing/chain_saga_neustria_west.json. Page: Design/content/chains/saga_neustria_west.md. Written 6 Oct 2026 from Design/content/dossiers/herio.md, namnetis.md, burdigala.md, rotomagus.md and parisius.md; a draft for the user to overwrite. It tells in full the story herio.saints_road of places/herio.json and keeps that story's three endings. Flags: ch_saga_neustria_west_<n> for the steps; the roads _road_saint, _road_hold, _road_island, _road_lead; _oil, _letter, _fought, _isl, _told, _provided, _abbot_cool, _marks, _marks_duty, _carried, _late, _carter, _lead_warned, _lead_back, _tithe, _saints_grudge, _book; the endings ch_saga_neustria_west_end_saint, _end_island, _end_held, _end_lead; the places file's herio_saint_carried; history changed: changed_herio_836.

cards.note: Step 1, the start (drawn at Herio or Namnetis, 830 to midsummer 835). The abbot is walling a house he empties every spring. Sources: the diploma of Louis and Lothar, 2 August 830, for Abbot Hilbod's castrum 'around the monastery', guarded by the abbey's own men; the monks at Deas from early spring to the end of autumn (Ermentarius, Miracles I.1; charter of 16 March 819); the monastery's lead taken off for fear of the Northmen and laid at Furca (Miracles I.81; when it was taken off is not said (?)); six abbey boats toll-free on the Loire (Pippin I, 18 May 826); the Bordeaux oil ship (Vita Filiberti); all as read in dossiers/herio.md. People: herio.hilbod (real), herio.natalis (invented). Sets ch_saga_neustria_west_1.

cards.note: Step 3 (Herio, August 835 for the day itself; until May 836 for the telling of it). The fight on the saint's feast. Cartron doubts the date and the number; the game keeps the day and lets the people doubt the number. People: namnetis.rainald (real), herio.hilbod (real), herio.martinus (invented). cards.note: Step 4, the turn (Namnetis, September 835 to May 836). Hilbod has leave to move the saint. Sources: Ermentarius, Miracles I.1: the abbot went to King Pippin (Pippin I of Aquitaine, died 838), whose assembly agreed the move; the reason given: because of the ebbs (ledones) 'our men' cannot always reach the island, and the Northmen can whenever the sea is calm; the fear that the tomb would be dug up and the bones scattered or thrown in the sea (dossiers/herio.md 1, 6). Gunhard, bishop of Nantes 835 to 843, and his friendship with Hilbod: places/namnetis.json (the friendship is that file's (?)). Where the assembly sat is not in the dossier (?); that Hilbod came home by Namnetis and that the count offered men are invented. People: namnetis.gunhard, herio.hilbod, namnetis.rainald (all real). Sets ch_saga_neustria_west_4 and one road: _road_saint, _road_hold or _road_island.

cards.note: Step 5 on the road _road_hold (Herio, before June 836). A trial before the count. Sources: the monastery's channel (alveus) dries at the ebb (Vita Filiberti 28); the king's council on the ebbs (Miracles I.1); horsemen fought on the island in 835 (Miracles II.11). Invented: the marks, the ferry, the trial, and that anyone offered it; withies to mark a channel are the common practice of tidal waters and are in no text of the bay (?). Martinus learned the ebbs from old Ursus (places/herio.json). Sets ch_saga_neustria_west_5; _marks on success; on failure _road_saint.

cards.note: Step 5 on the road _road_island (Herio, before June 836). The islanders. Sources: the islanders (insulani) had a lord of their own and were not the monks' people; they still lived on the island about 838 to 840 (Miracles I.1, I.81); the island 'never wholly without a few monks' (Falco 22); dossiers/herio.md 1, 5. Invented: the three heaps and their sharing, what was told and by whom, and what the abbot left; the beat is that of places/herio.json, story herio.saints_road ('They are not coming to Deas. Nobody has asked them.'). People: herio.martinus, herio.natalis (invented). Sets ch_saga_neustria_west_5; _told; _abbot_cool (a lasting cost); or _provided with _road_saint (the hard and honest road).

cards.note: Step 6, an offer that can be refused (Namnetis, October 835 to June 836, after the council). The monks' lead. Sources: Ermentarius, Miracles I.81: about 838 to 840 Breton ships with yards, sails and anchors came to Furca 'to trade', having brought grain and carrying away 'only salt'; the monastery's lead lay there for fear of the Northmen, and a Breton crew took some, 'partly by theft, partly by buying on the quiet'; their ship had a steersman (gubernator) and a bow lookout (proreta) (dossiers/herio.md 3, 4). The game moves the theft two to four years earlier, to before the saint's going (?). Riwal is invented: a Breton name of the Redon charters (Riuual), from memory (?). There is no Breton people or tongue in the tables: he is given 'romance' here (see the report's needs). Sets ch_saga_neustria_west_6; _road_lead, or _lead_warned.

cards.note: Step 7, the day (Herio, June 836; a house that comes later, to 842, finds the pit in the floor). Sources: Ermentarius, Miracles I.2: the tomb dug out on 7 June 836 and the body shipped in its marble coffin from the island to Furca, a fast run before a north-west wind, then carried on men's shoulders by Ampan, Varenne and Paulx to Deas, 7 to 11 June; the coffin's carrying frame (scala); three lamps at the head of the tomb (II.8); 'never wholly without a few monks' (Falco 22); the stolen lead came back as sheets and was recast in lumps (I.81): dossiers/herio.md. Easter 836 fell on 9 April, so 7 June is the tenth day after Pentecost (our reckoning (?)). Whose ship carried the saint is not written: that is the room the player stands in. People: herio.hilbod, herio.ermentarius (real), herio.martinus (invented). Sets ch_saga_neustria_west_7; _carried with herio_saint_carried; _late; or _carter.

cards.note: ENDING 1, what happened: the saint on the mainland (Namnetis, a month after the day). Sources: the body reached Deas on 11 June 836, with cures along the road; women admitted to Deas for one year, feast to feast (Miracles I.2, I.29, I.71); the abbey's six toll-free boats (Pippin I, 826); the six pounds of silver owed yearly to the royal chamber (diploma of 830); the frame (scala) the coffin was carried on (I.2); Gunhard defended Hilbod when people called it faint heart (places/namnetis.json (?)): dossiers/herio.md. The guest right, the room in the boats and the sums are invented, and are the unlock herio.saints_guest of places/herio.json. Sets ch_saga_neustria_west_end_saint and one grand reward: unlock_title_guest_of_saint_philibert, unlock_charter_namnetis, both the title and unlock_factor_herio (the hard road), or unlock_upgrade_rollers_tackle.

cards.note: ENDING 3, HISTORY CHANGED: the saint stays behind a manned wall (Herio, from the saint's feast of 836). What happened: the council judged that the ebbs kept the count's men off the island, and the body was moved on 7 June 836 (Miracles I.1 to I.2); it went on to Cunault (858), Messay (862) and Tournus (875), and Herio burned in July 846 (Annals of Angouleme). Here the channel is marked, a ferry lies at Furca and the count keeps men on the wall: all invented. The page says what would follow. cards.note: ENDING 4: the monks' lead sold on the Seine (Rotomagus, ten to fourteen days after the calm). Sources: Philibert founded Jumieges, below Rouen, about 654, before he was driven out and built on Herio about 675 (Vita Filiberti; dossiers/herio.md 1; the year 654 from memory (?)); his feast, 20 August; lead wanted for church roofs in Neustria (goods_793.json; Gervold roofed two churches with lead, Gesta of Fontenelle). In Ermentarius the lead came back (Miracles I.81): here the player may sell it. The cellarer of Jumieges is invented and unnamed; that Jumieges bought lead at Rouen in 836 is invented. Sets ch_saga_neustria_west_end_lead and unlock_partner_riwal or unlock_factor_rotomagus; a lasting cost, ch_saga_neustria_west_saints_grudge, unless the tithe is paid or the truth told.

cards.note: The coda, after any ending (Parisius, 838 to 840). The first book of the Miracles. Sources: Ermentarius wrote book I about 838 to 840 and sent it to Hilduin, abbot of Saint-Denis (814 to 840/841), to be corrected (Poupardin 1905, as in dossiers/herio.md 3); Hilduin's chapel of 832 where eight monks sang day and night, and Saint-Denis buying parchment (dossiers/parisius.md; the spine's book_road); the 484 dead (Miracles II.11, which is in book II, written after 862: the game lets Hilduin hear the number early (?)); the lead thieves (I.81). People: parisius.hilduin (real). That Hilduin questioned a shipman is invented. Sets ch_saga_neustria_west_book.
